disposition: Applied production ASTs exactly match independently reviewed proposals; no new concrete static defect identified in the bounded change. Current-source parity, browser and full release qualification remain separate pending gates.
guard_review: Graph status is captured after _load_state under the existing graph FileLock. All three refresh branches return their locally captured immutable status along with the original refresh result.
Existing public refresh/rebuild retain GraphRefreshResult through the wrapper; no status is stored as shared mutable engine state.

Builder obtains graph/HEAD/branch/full dirty paths from the same refresh observation, retaining non-graph dirty paths before the original .orqalis filtering. Ranking, freshness checks, budgets and fitting remain unchanged.
Root/common-directory/storage and graph cache/schema/parser/digest checks remain those of the reviewed implementation; shared status does not bypass them.

Git status retains root/_execute dispatch, inherited GIT override stripping, hooks/fsmonitor suppression, optional lock behavior and timeout. It uses no-ahead-behind, preserves raw NUL filenames and rejects incomplete framing/duplicate required known headers.
No mtime shortcuts or new result cache; external Git/filesystem changes remain best-effort observations, not a filesystem transaction.
compatibility_and_cost_limits: LocalGitService.status no longer dispatches resolve_commit(root, HEAD); a third-party subclass relying only on that override changes behavior. No repository subclass relying on it was identified. Root and _execute overrides remain preserved.
Custom ProjectGraphEngine subclasses overriding only refresh no longer customize builder refresh_with_status; builder normally owns its engine and injected GitService is preserved.
Private _refresh_locked return shape changes; public existing refresh/rebuild result contracts remain unchanged.

Porcelain v2 includes more metadata per dirty record than v1; decoded stdout and split records therefore create larger temporary allocations, including an extra sliced list for excluding the trailing empty element. No allocation bound or peak-memory reduction is claimed; no persistent status cache is introduced.

Two Git subprocesses replace four within LocalGitService.status, and builder uses one refresh status instead of a separate status call. This is an algorithmic call-count reduction, not measured browser latency cure.
Validation claim is limited to framing, record field extraction, nonempty paths and required header values; complete unused Git metadata grammar is not validated.
